candidates.question:
$[AB]$ is a chord of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $10$ cm.
$|AB| = 16$ cm.
Find the distance from $O$ to the chord $AB$.

lines.text: The perpendicular from the centre $O$ to the chord meets it at its midpoint $M$ (Theorem 21).
$OMA$ has a right angle at $M$ and hypotenuse $|OA| = 10$.

candidates.question:
A circle has centre $O$ and radius $13$ cm.
$M$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $O$ to a chord $[PQ]$, and $|OM| = 5$ cm.
Find $|PQ|$.

lines.text: $OM \perp PQ$, so $OMP$ has a right angle at $M$ and hypotenuse $|OP| = 13$.
The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord (Theorem 21), so $M$ is the midpoint of $[PQ]$.

candidates.question:
A horizontal pipe has a circular cross-section.
The surface of the water in the pipe is a chord of the circle of length $48$ cm.
The water is $8$ cm deep at its deepest point, which is directly below the midpoint of the chord.
Find the radius of the pipe.

lines.text: Let $O$ be the centre and $r$ the radius. The line from $O$ to the midpoint $M$ of the chord is perpendicular to the chord (Theorem 21), so it is the vertical line through the deepest point.
Half the chord is $24$ cm, and $|OM| = r - 8$.

steps.title: Use Pythagoras in the triangle with sides $r$, $24$ and $r-8$

candidates.question:
In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = 9$ cm, $|BC| = 7$ cm and $|AC| = 5$ cm. The three angles of the triangle measure $33^\circ$, $52^\circ$ and $95^\circ$ in some order.
Find $\angle ABC$.

steps.title: Match each side to its opposite angle

lines.text: $|AB|$ is opposite $\angle ACB$, $|BC|$ is opposite $\angle BAC$ and $|AC|$ is opposite $\angle ABC$.
$|AC|$ is the shortest side.
The smaller side is opposite the smaller angle, so $|AC|$ is opposite the smallest angle.

candidates.question:
In triangle $DEF$, $|DE| > |DF| > |EF|$. The three angles of the triangle measure $34^\circ$, $62^\circ$ and $84^\circ$ in some order.
Find $\angle DEF$.

steps.title: Match each side to its opposite angle

lines.text: $|DE|$ is opposite $\angle DFE$, $|DF|$ is opposite $\angle DEF$ and $|EF|$ is opposite $\angle EDF$.
The greatest side is opposite the greatest angle, so $\angle DFE = 84^\circ$.
The least side $|EF|$ is opposite the least angle, so $\angle EDF = 34^\circ$.
$|DF|$ is the middle side, so $\angle DEF$ is the middle angle.

candidates.question:

lines.text: The angles in a triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
The greatest side is opposite the greatest angle, so the angle opposite the longest side is $\angle B$.
